 Big Story Features Delhi Bengal Nation Opinion Editorial World Business Sports Entertainment Sponsored All Authors Home >  Nation >  Diwali crackers push air quality to ‘hazardous’ levels across UP Nation Diwali crackers push air quality to ‘hazardous’ levels across UP 
 BY  Biswajeet Banerjee 9 Nov 2026 11:37 PM IST X Biswajeet Banerjee 9 Nov 2026 11:37 PM IST 
 Lucknow: Diwali celebrations left a trail of toxic air across Uttar Pradesh, with several cities recording alarming levels of pollution after hours of fireworks. Aligarh emerged as one of the worst-affected cities, with its Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 606 around 11 pm on Diwali night, putting the air in the hazardous category.
 The post-Diwali pollution spike was particularly worrying as several parts of the state were already witnessing deteriorating air quality ahead of the festival. Firecracker emissions added to the existing pollution load, pushing concentrations of fine particulate matter and other harmful pollutants to dangerous levels. 
 The impact was not confined to Aligarh. Meerut, Ghaziabad, Baghpat and Muzaffarnagar also recorded high pollution levels on Monday morning, indicating that the festive emissions had affected a wide stretch of western Uttar Pradesh. 
 In Lucknow, the deterioration was equally concerning. The city’s air quality had already slipped into the poor category before Diwali, with an average AQI of 223 recorded on November 7, according to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data. The situation worsened after the festival. The average AQI rose to 315 on November 8, while the Talkatora monitoring station recorded a reading of 500 on November 9. 
 The post-Diwali readings from different monitoring platforms painted an alarming picture of pollution across the state. According to AQI.in data reported on Monday, Prayagraj recorded an AQI of 633, Faizabad 781 and Bahraich 575. Other cities reporting readings above 300 included Agra (310), Aligarh (319), Amethi (304), Baghpat (477), Bareilly (312), Badaun (330), Bulandshahr (333) and Etawah (366). 
 CPCB figures also showed high pollution levels in several cities. Ghaziabad recorded an AQI of 366, Noida 340, Varanasi 302 and Bulandshahr 371. Greater Noida stood at 293, Hapur at 255, Gorakhpur at 261 and Kanpur at 221. 
 The readings, however, need to be seen in the context of different monitoring platforms and AQI scales. CPCB classifies readings between 401 and 500 as severe, while some private platforms use the hazardous and extreme categories for higher readings. 
 Doctors warned that exposure to such high levels of pollution could trigger respiratory problems, particularly among children, elderly people and those suffering from asthma and other lung diseases. 
 Former Medical Officer of Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow Dr S K Pandey, said severe air pollution could cause irritation in the respiratory tract, persistent coughing, breathlessness and asthma attacks. People with existing respiratory ailments needed to take extra precautions, he said.
